current_date: Updated June 2026 (document cover/headers); web page last modified 24/06/2026
current_evidence: The council's 'Local list of information requirements' page (spelthorne.gov.uk/page/1039, also /article/17694) links only this PDF (699 KB, 2026-06 folder) and no older or newer version; the document text says 'updated June 2026'.

issues.detail: Status not recorded. The council page presents the June 2026 list as the subject of a four-week consultation (11 June to 9 July 2026) and never says it has been adopted or when it takes effect. Grokbot marks it 'Captured' with no caveat. It is still the only list the council publishes, so the link is current, but adoption should be confirmed.
issues.evidence: Planning page: consultation on the 'Local List of Requirements (June 2026)' 'will run for four weeks, from 11 June 2026 to 9 July 2026'

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none) - national requirements only'. That is wrong. The list sets several items for 'All applications' or 'All planning applications', including householder: Item 13 Design Code checklist, Item 33 SuDS statement/pro forma and Item 39 Climate Change Checklist (the SPD has a householder version). Conditional items also catch extensions: Item 9 levels/sections (roof extensions and dormers), Item 19 FRA (residential extensions in flood zones), Item 30 tree survey and Item 5 adjoining-property window plans.
issues.evidence: Item 13 'All applications'; Item 33 'All planning applications are required to demonstrate...'; Item 39 'All Planning Applications' / 'one for householder applications, one for minor applications'

issues.detail: About 28 requirements carry the note 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. The list has a 'Types of application' column for every item, and Grokbot ignored it. As a result, requirements that apply to all applications (Design Code checklist, SuDS, Climate Change Checklist, CIL form) appear only under Full planning. Items limited to LBC/CA works (Item 21 Heritage, Item 37 Structural survey) are also put under Full planning, and Works to trees shows '(none)'.
issues.evidence: Each item table has 'Types of application that require this information'

issues.detail: Three requirements are put under the wrong application types. Lighting Assessment goes under Listed building consent, but Item 22's trigger is 'Application for floodlighting'. Contaminated Land goes under 'Minerals & waste (county)', but Item 18 applies to development on or next to previously developed or contaminated land, and to 10+ dwellings. BNG appears only under Outline, but Item 38 says 'All'.
issues.evidence: Item 22 'Application for floodlighting'; Item 18 'Applications which propose development on or adjacent to land that has been subject to previous industrial or commercial uses'; Item 38 'All'

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts were pasted from the wrong item. 'Archaeological Assessment' carries the foul sewage/utilities text ('availability of utility services has been examined...'). 'Waste / Refuse storage' carries the planning obligations Heads of Terms text. 'Travel Plan' runs on into the tree survey note. 'Daylight/Sunlight' ends with the LLFA SuDS sentence. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' carries the Construction Management Plan text.
issues.evidence: Item 21 trigger: 'Applications for Listed Building or Conservation Area Consent' (sites of high archaeological potential, 0.4ha+)

issues.detail: Several triggers are only table column headings or fragments, with no actual trigger. Flood Risk Assessment, Ecological Survey (PEA), HRA/SPA, Ventilation/extraction, Planning Obligations and Design Code all show 'Policy driver Types of application ... Spelthorne Local Plan 2024-2039/40'. Drainage/SuDS shows just 'consultee for SuDS.' The real triggers are missing: FRA applies in Flood Zones 2/3/3b and surface-water risk areas, for new dwellings/conversions, residential extensions in FZ3b and sites over 0.5ha / 10+ dwellings / 1,000 sq m. PEA applies to designated sites (SSSI/SNCI/SPA), major development or land within 100m of priority habitat. Ventilation applies to commercial kitchens and Class E food uses.
issues.evidence: Item 19 'Residential development created by new build or conversion' in Flood Zones 2 and 3; Item 16 PEA triggers

issues.detail: The Structural Survey and Foul sewage triggers come from the old-style explanatory notes ('17) Structural Survey ... barn conversion'), not the operative item table. Item 37 limits a structural survey to Listed Building applications and Conservation Area applications involving demolition or part demolition. The Fire Statement excerpt leaves out the 18m / 7+ storey, 2+ dwellings threshold.
issues.evidence: Item 37 'Listed Building and applications and applications within a Conservation Area that propose the demolition or partial demolition of buildings'

issues.detail: Local items in the source that Grokbot did not capture at all: Item 14 Accessibility Compliance Statement (new dwellings, M4(2)/M4(3)); Item 23 Noise assessment (noise-generating development or noise-sensitive uses near noise sources); Item 35 Wind microclimate study (buildings over 6 storeys); Item 27 Waste and Recycling Strategy (major, 10+ units or flatted); Item 40 Tree sketch/location plan (works to TPO trees or trees in Conservation Areas); Item 5 plans of adjoining properties' windows (built development adjoining homes); Item 8 Roof plans (new buildings and extensions with complex roofs); Item 10 manufacturer's details of listed building features (LBC).

Item 12, the Affordable Housing Viability Statement, applies to 10+ dwellings (at least 30% affordable, 50% on greenfield), but Grokbot's 'Viability Assessment' row gives no threshold. Item 15 Air Quality Assessment applies to 10+ dwellings or 1,000 sq m+ non-residential, and the whole borough is an AQMA. Grokbot's air quality excerpt has no threshold.
issues.evidence: Item 12 '10+ dwellings'; Item 15 'Whole borough is an AQMA'

issues.detail: 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' is listed as a requirement, but the source only says information 'might form part of an Environmental Statement, where one is necessary' in the explanatory notes. It is not a local list item. The Construction Management Plan likewise appears only inside Explanatory Note 2 (air quality), not as a numbered item, so its 'must be submitted where development involves demolition' trigger overstates it.
issues.evidence: Explanatory Notes 2-4; no EIA or CMP item in Items 1-40

issues.detail: Three tab_items under 'Drawing / document standards' repeat the same 'Plans should be in PDF format ... annotated with the overall dimensions' sentence, and a fourth under 'Submission rules' repeats 'Plans should be in PDF format'. One of them includes the table header fragment 'Geographic locations where this information is required What information is required Where to look for further assistance'.

The 'Policy-driven requirements' tab item (PEA) is garbled. The text is spliced with the 'Where to look' column ('NPPF', 'Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981', 'Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2010') and cannot be read as a trigger. The Design Code tab item says 'All applications for new dwellings', but Item 13 says 'All applications'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the only Spelthorne local list published (June 2026), but the council page presents it as a consultation version with no adoption date. The extraction is weak: only 7 tab items, Householder wrongly set to 'none', many triggers that are column headers or text from other items, and about 8 local items missing (accessibility, noise, wind, waste strategy, TPO tree plan and others).
